rule: runnable *.py/*.sh; skip __pycache__, results/, *.bak*, *.config.sh; description = own header (python docstring or leading # block), usable if >= 40 chars and >= 6 words; no LLM, never invented

items.description: deploy.sh — ONE comprehensive, self-diagnosing deploy you run on YOUR Mac. It does exactly what your working terminal does, but bundled, safe, and with a full report at the end. Two clearly separated phases: PHASE A (read-only) — gather system facts: creds, tools, network, VM reach. PHASE B (real update) — rsync local -> VM as `mostafa`, then build on the VM. It NEVER touches secrets / node_modules / .env / prisma migrations / public / uploads / build output. It does NOT use `rsync --delete` by default (no data loss). Every step records its exit code + output; a summary table prints last. USAGE: bash infra/deploy.sh # full deploy (backend + frontend) bash infra/deploy.sh --dry-run # rsync dry-run (shows what WOULD sync), no build bash infra/deploy.sh backend # only the backend target bash infra/deploy.sh frontend src/components # sync only a SUBFOLDER of frontend Run it once, paste me the report it prints, and I fix whatever it surfaces.

Deployment change-detection — the FIRST step the DevOps agent runs before any organics deploy. Keeps TWO saved lists (front-end + back-end) built from the owner's LOCAL source folders: - VolatileWorkSpace/RBO-Staging/f (staging frontend) - VolatileWorkSpace/RBO-Staging/b (staging backend) Each list records every deployable file + its **modification date** (mtime), EXCLUDING the things we never deploy: node_modules, .env / .env.* / .backup-env, build folders (.next front / dist back), package.json + the lockfile, and public/uploads/logs. On each deploy the agent: 1) `scan` → compares current mtimes to the saved list → prints added / modified / removed. If a baseline exists and NOTHING changed → deployment is NOT required (skip). 2) deploys ONLY the changed files (over SSH as mostafa; az only for firewall/IP; never root). 3) after a VERIFIED-successful deploy → `update` → saves the current **real** mtimes as the new baseline. Special one-time bootstrap (`seed-old`): when there is no reliable prior state, write the baseline with every file's date set to 2 years ago, so the very next `scan` reports EVERYTHING as changed → a full, clean overwrite happens through the NORMAL script flow (no hardcoded exception). After that deploy succeeds, `update` records the real dates so future runs detect real changes only. python infra/deploy_changes.py scan # front+back diff vs saved lists python infra/deploy_changes.py seed-old # one-time: baseline dated 2 years ago (=> all changed) python in

deploy_run.sh — the ONE command the organics-prod-deploy PROJECT/agent runs. It chains the full, correct flow with strong gates. The agent runs THIS, not a pile of manual commands. Order is fixed and each stage gates the next: STEP 0 CHANGE DETECTION → python infra/deploy_changes.py scan • no changes (baseline exists) → STOP, "no deployment required". • changes → continue (deploy only what changed). STEP 1 DEPLOY → bash "$HERE"/deploy.sh (rsync as mostafa → migrate(reset|new) → build → restart bendcore-staging+organics-staging [the reboot solution, no full VM reboot]). STEP 2 STRONG VERIFY → python infra/deploy_verify.py --since-epoch <deploy start> • REAL file change on VM (fresh dist + .next/BUILD_ID), :4014 & :3001 == 200, DB users>0/roles>0/superadmin>0/appSettings>0. Auto-restart-once if DB empty. • FAIL → STOP, do NOT update lists, report ❌ (never fake success). STEP 3 UPDATE LISTS → python infra/deploy_changes.py update (REAL current mtimes, to the minute) • only on a PASS, so a re-run says "no deployment required". STEP 4 CONFIRM DONE. Rules honored: SSH as mostafa; az ONLY for the SSH firewall; never root for app work; never touch nginx/ports/other sites; never `npm run start`. bash infra/deploy_run.sh # normal run bash infra/deploy_run.sh --bootstrap # seed change-lists to 2-years-ago first (=> everything changed)

Post-deploy STRONG VERIFICATION — the mandatory gate the DevOps agent runs after every organics deploy. The deploy is NOT "done" until this prints VERDICT: ✅ PASS. It NEVER fakes success. WHY (real incidents 2026-07-16): - `migrate reset --force` dropped every table under the still-running process; the deploy skipped the restart, so the boot self-seed never re-ran → DB EMPTY (users=0) yet the OLD process still answered HTTP 200 → "You do not have permission" on every login. HTTP 200 is NOT proof of a good deploy. - The health check curled the WRONG port (3000 instead of the real organics port 3001) and never checked the frontend BUILD_ID, so a STALE build (08:44, from before the deploy) passed as "healthy". STRONG CHECKPOINTS (all over SSH as mostafa — never root, never touch nginx/ports, never `npm start`): 1. REAL FILE CHANGE ON VM — backend `dist/` and frontend `.next/BUILD_ID` must be FRESH (rebuilt within the deploy window). A stale build fails. This proves the code actually changed on the VM. 2. SMART ENDPOINTS — poll backend :4014 and frontend :3001 (the REAL organics port) to a real HTTP 200. 3. DB HEALTH — users>0, rbacRoles>0, at least one isSuperadmin=true, appSettings seeded (captcha config). 4. AUTO-REMEDIATE ONCE — if DB is empty but services are up, restart bendcore (boot self-seed refills), wait, re-check. (Restart after a reset is the step that re-runs the seed.) Ports are READ-ONLY here (curl only). This script never edits nginx, ports, or firewall. python i

ensure-connection.sh — SAFE, idempotent connection restore + health check. It ONLY ever OPENS the ports the public sites need and REPORTS status. It NEVER denies, flushes, resets, disables, or restarts anything — so running it can NOT break functionality or security. Run it on the VM any time a site seems unreachable; it brings the web ports back and tells you the real state. (SSH/port-22 single-IP tightening is a separate, deliberate action — not done here, so this can never lock you out.)

phase3_e2e.py — smart PRODUCTION end-to-end checks for Phase 3. Purpose: isolate the ONE real risk of Phase 3 — the switch from development to production configuration (URLs, ports, deployed paths, cloud latency). Phase 2 already proved the behaviour; here we prove the ONLINE endpoints answer correctly with production config and no accidental direct-backend dependency. Each check has a FIXED expectation. Exit 0 = all critical checks pass; non-zero = a real failure. Reads only; sends nothing that mutates state.

phase3_gate.py — the SAFE decision brain for Phase 3 deployment. It never touches Phase 2, the development configuration, or the original successful folders. It only: * maintains DEPLOYMENT COPIES of the successful anchor + web folders (deploy_anchor/, deploy_web/) * compares the originals against those copies * manages a FIRST-RUN flag so the very first deployment always happens (even with no diff), and later runs skip when nothing changed / ask when something changed * runs READ-ONLY VM validation (SSH, reverse proxy, SSL/domain, paths, PostgreSQL, env, firewall) * snapshots the copies + stamps the first-run flag only AFTER a successful deploy Subcommands (exit codes are meaningful so the shell can branch without parsing text): init ensure deploy_anchor/deploy_web exist (creating them = first run). exit 0 compare print SAME|CHANGED|FIRST_RUN + details. exit 0=SAME 10=CHANGED 20=FIRST_RUN validate read-only VM checks. exit 0=ok 1=blocking problem (e.g. SSH down) snapshot copy originals -> deploy copies + write fingerprints + stamp first-run flag. exit 0 Design rules honored: - originals are READ ONLY here; only deploy_* copies are written - first run MUST deploy even if identical; only after success is the flag set - never recreate DB / SSL / services — validate reports existence, deploy creates only if missing - never weaken firewall (validation is read-only; the dynamic-IP SSH rule is refreshed by deploy_ssh)
Entry point so the whole suite runs by calling the folder: python3 testing/ (or python3 -m testing). Delegates to run_all.py, which auto-discovers and runs every test (current and future).

REAL end-to-end driver for the Zoom Smart Meeting Notification Agent. Drives the SAME HTTP endpoints the web/mobile/desktop UI calls — no shortcut functions: 1) POST /projects/intake (paste the spec as the owner would) -> CTO proposes a TEAM 2) assert NO deviation (only the brief's own agents; no Fulfillment/Frontend/Backend/QA/DevOps) 3) POST /projects (create with the proposed spec) -> team is seeded 4) GET /agents/all (created agents visible org-wide) 5) POST /projects/{id}/run-now (the play button path) -> autonomous run, fills the chat Run: python testing/e2e_real_flow.py

Strong E2E for RedBerry Continuous SOC — approves NOTHING, makes NO production change. Runs from the agent bridge shell. Asserts agent coordination, safety, detection, false-positives, memorizing tracker, multi-format reporting, and the mandatory auto-remediation guard.

testing/harness.py — the shared core for Odin's restructured E2E suite. Every test in this folder uses these helpers so behavior is consistent: • smart_timeout() — reasonable (not aggressive) per-test time limits, scaled by complexity. • SeedingPrompt — AFTER each test (pass OR fail) asks: clean up the test data, or KEEP it as seeding for future work? (honors ODIN_TEST_KEEP / ODIN_TEST_CLEAN env for non-interactive CI runs.) • auto_resolve_dialogs() — during a test, if the CTO raises a capability gap / unknown-agent dialog, resolve it intelligently (pick the best existing agent, else let the CTO handle it) so the test never blocks waiting on a human. • assert_cto_present() — the CTO must always be present/visible, even on an "only X" project. Shared context pool is preserved: tests drive the SAME scope pool the app uses; nothing here bypasses or trims the shared history.

isolate_anchor.py — ONE NODE, PROVEN 100%. We do NOT redeploy and we do NOT move on until every single transmission TO and FROM the anchor is verified, timing included. This runs on the Mac (external, over public HTTPS) so it mimics EXACTLY what the web/mobile app does — same URLs, same headers, same order. It answers, with evidence, the three doubts: (1) Is the anchor reachable and does its DATA come back correctly (forward read)? → T1..T3 (2) What EXACTLY causes the app's "HTTP 404 error page"? (a 404 has ONE meaning: wrong link) → T4 (3) Is the async queue real: FAST ACK now ("received/queued"), then the local machine pulls, processes, and the RESULT returns later (webhook + acknowledgement) — never a synchronous 502? → T5 Every transmission prints: the exact request, the exact response (status + head of body + key headers), the elapsed time, and a hard PASS/PROBLEM verdict. A final VERDICT block says whether the ANCHOR NODE is 100% or names the first transmission that failed.

Odin autonomous test LOOP — execution host on YOUR machine that the agent fully controls via files. Start ONCE (you can close the terminal if you use nohup): nohup bash testing/loop.sh > testing/results/daemon.log 2>&1 & The AGENT controls everything through the shared workspace folder — no babysitting: • touch/echo into testing/results/RUN_NOW → (re)START a run. Content = filter word ("all", "shipping", "email", "revealer", "real", …). If a run is in progress it is STOPPED first, then a fresh one starts (so new code is always picked up). • touch testing/results/STOP → STOP the current run immediately. • results land in testing/results/latest.log + STATUS + RUN_SEQ (the agent reads these). AUTONOMOUS loop CLEANS data after each test (ODIN_TEST_CLEAN=1) for correct fresh behavior every trial. (When YOU run `python3 testing/` yourself, you instead get the keep/clean prompt.) Test 1 stays propose-only unless ODIN_TEST_PROD_DEPLOY=1 is exported before starting.

Odin LIVE MONITOR — open this ONCE in its own terminal and LEAVE IT. It NEVER closes on its own: • `tail -F` (capital F) follows the log BY NAME, so it survives the log being truncated/replaced every time the agent (re)starts a run — plain `tail -f` dies on that; this does not. • the `while true` wrapper RELAUNCHES tail if it ever exits for any reason, so the view is permanent. You just watch here, live, alongside the agent (step markers → starting step N/M, the heartbeat working… Ns, per-step results, scorecards, final verdict). Close it only when YOU want to (Cmd-W).

phase7_lib.py — the SHARED per-project test logic (Phase 7). One home for the test body; every project's tests/project_test.py is a thin pointer that calls run_project_test(<its id>). That is the anti-duplication model applied to the tests themselves: the capability lives in shared/, each consumer reuses it with its own id — no copy per project. A child test confirms a project is CORRECT and CONSISTENT with the new architecture, fast: 1. canonical skeleton present (folders + index.json valid), 2. present + seeded in odin_core, 3. every on-disk file is indexed (DB lockstep), 4. no schema/cross-owner violations for this project (uses the audit's own detectors), 5. capability integrity — every dependency resolves to a real shared/ capability (not a bundled copy, not a foreign project path). Live external execution is a later layer (after the anchor); this proves structural + capability health with a performance number, which is what must be green BEFORE anything heavier runs.

phase7_lifecycle.py — the create → monitor → clean cycle (Phase 7). Creates 4 NEW projects via the NEW methodology (workspace_mw.create_owner — the single door), each a different shape, MONITORS the system after each create (middleware placement + odin_core lockstep + audit == 0 violations), then DELETES them via delete_owner and proves the system returns to EXACT baseline while any promoted SHARED capability survives. Shapes: 1. schedule — recurring/periodical scheduled project 2. reader — read-only connector reader 3. deploy — REUSES the shared deploy capability via request_capability (proves NO deploy_2 duplicate) 4. revealer — multi-agent project (links several existing agents) Production (organics/bendcore) is never touched. Run: python3 workspace/shared/testing/phase7_lifecycle.py

phase7_monitor.py — the PARENT test (Phase 7): the monitor that runs each project's child test and, AFTER each one, exercises the SYSTEM and asserts it stayed correct: • middleware placement — no file of this project sits in the wrong schema slot, • odin_core lockstep — every on-disk file is indexed, • audit — running the audit ('run now') finds + heals, converging to ZERO violations, • structure — nothing leaked outside the project / into another owner. The role here is MONITOR, not player: the middleware + audit are what keep things correct; this harness proves they do, from several angles, and reports it. Production (organics/bendcore) is EXCLUDED — never touched. Run: python3 workspace/shared/testing/phase7_monitor.py

phase7_prompt4.py — the OWNER JOURNEY, strong: create 4 NEW projects BY PROMPT (as the owner), each mixing several existing capabilities/agents, then for each project prove — with STRONG acceptance points baked into the check (not into the system) — that: 1. the system PLANNED from the prompt (intake), 2. CREATE seeded the RIGHT team and it is visible on every DB-backed surface (project_agents JOIN — the exact query ui_api.py + directions.py use for the desktop/web/mobile cards), 3. capability REUSE happened where the brief needed a shared capability (deploy -> shared/, NOT a copy), 4. RUN produced REAL output (message growth) — the project actually does its task, 5. ZERO general + ZERO cross-owner violations for the project (audit is the judge, healed first), 6. DELETE returns the system to EXACT baseline (every count) — clean, modular teardown. The 4 specs deliberately MIX HubSpot CRM, Veeqo fulfillment, Klaviyo email, SOC/security, reporting/export and deployment so the run also proves REUSE (shared + custom delta) instead of re-creation. Run: python3 workspace/shared/testing/phase7_prompt4.py Exit 0 only if ALL four are fully clean AND global violations end at 0.

phase7_prompt_loop.py — the USER journey, automated: send a PROMPT, let the system plan, approve, watch it build, audit, then delete — measuring the time from prompt → output. For each spec: 1. POST /projects/intake with the prompt (the system derives the plan / asks for enhancement) 2. approve the proposal (we act as the owner and accept) 3. POST /projects to actually create it (full stack: CTO + inferred team + connectors) 4. WATCH until it produces output <-- TIMED WINDOW (prompt -> expected output) 5. AUDIT (manual run) + middleware placement + DB lockstep + cross/general violations 6. DELETE it and prove other agents/projects are untouched (exact baseline restore) The specs deliberately MIX existing capabilities (HubSpot CRM, Veeqo fulfillment, Klaviyo email, SOC/security, scheduling) so the run also proves capability REUSE instead of re-creation. Run: python3 workspace/shared/testing/phase7_prompt_loop.py

phase7_realrun.py — REAL first-time run of every project, timed, with audit+middleware monitoring. For each project (production organics/bendcore EXCLUDED): 1. snapshot DB + violations BEFORE 2. trigger the project's REAL run through the brain (SOC -> /soc/run, others -> /projects/<pid>/run-now) 3. wait until it actually produces output (scope-message quiescence) — this is the TIMED window 4. run the AUDIT ('run now') + middleware placement + DB-lockstep checks 5. report: description, what it does, result, DURATION, gaps found/solved Usage: python3 workspace/shared/testing/phase7_realrun.py # all projects python3 workspace/shared/testing/phase7_realrun.py <pid> ... # only these

phase7_strong.py — the STRONG, adversarial Phase-7 test. Not twisted to pass: it INJECTS every violation type and proves the system CORRECTS it for real (files actually move, DB rows change, source is rewritten), proves promote-to-shared + the pointer resolves to a LOADABLE capability, and proves custom-over-shared by EXECUTING the overlay. Ends by asserting 0 cross-owner AND 0 general violations, then restores baseline. Every check asserts the REAL outcome on disk / in the DB / in behavior — if the system fails to correct, the test raises and fails. Run: python3 workspace/shared/testing/phase7_strong.py

preflight.py — FAST, CHEAP health gate. Run this BEFORE committing to any expensive multi-agent build. The whole point of the new methodology: never again burn an hour (and tokens) only to discover a structural problem that a 10-second check would have caught — e.g. the Fullstack agent lacking write permission, a missing credential, a role that doesn't resolve, or a CTO that plans the wrong order. Preflight validates the SYSTEM is healthy and behaving logically, defines what we EXPECT, and returns a clear GO / NO-GO. Only on GO do we spend tokens on the real run. It checks, in order (cheapest first): 1) ENGINE + TOOLS — claude available; BUILD agents have Write/Edit/Bash; QA is read-only. 2) CREDENTIALS/ENV — oth/.cred exists and holds the keys the brief's integrations need. 3) ROLES — every requested role resolves and has a Resources & Dependencies section. 4) PLAN (optional, one cheap haiku call) — the CTO plans the RIGHT roles in the RIGHT order (requirements→Fullstack→QA→DevOps→operators→verify), with NO no-op steps. Graded by evaluate_plan. Usage: python3 testing/preflight.py # checks 1-3 (no token cost) python3 testing/preflight.py --plan "<brief>" # also does the cheap plan dry-run python3 testing/preflight.py --keys VEEQO,KLAVIYO # require these keys present Exit 0 = GO (healthy), 1 = NO-GO (stop and fix before spending tokens).

test_3_email_klaviyo_readonly.py — Test 3: Email marketing via Klaviyo. READ-ONLY. Real user flow: create an Email project that asks ONLY for the Email agent (Klaviyo); CTO is the manager (always present). No DevOps or any other agent. The project READS: number of live workflows, draft workflows, total workflows, plus metrics and lists. Nothing is sent or changed.

test_2_shipping_vq_readonly.py — Test 2: Shipping / Fulfillment provider (VQ / Veeqo). READ-ONLY. Real user flow: create a Fulfillment project that asks ONLY for the Shipping agent (VQ); CTO is the manager (always present). NO folder is required — the test proves the app does not block when no folder is selected. The project only READS from the external provider: connection status, total order count, channels/vendors, and confirms it's ready to answer future per-order status requests. Nothing is written.

run_all.py — ONE command to run EVERY test in this folder and bring back all results. Auto-discovers tests: any *.py in testing/ that defines a `main()` (except this runner, harness, and __init__). Future tests are picked up automatically — just drop a new file here with a `main()`. - Runs each test in sequence, in a sensible order (known tests first, then any new ones). - Each test prints its own STRONG scorecard; this runner adds a final aggregate SUMMARY (pass/fail + duration per test) and exits non-zero if anything failed. - Keeps all created data by default (seeding) so results can be fetched — override with ODIN_TEST_CLEAN=1. - Test 1 stays safe (propose-only) unless you set ODIN_TEST_PROD_DEPLOY=1 for the real production deploy. Run from the repo root: python3 testing/run_all.py

sandbox_deploy_overwrite_check.py — Test 5: DEVOPS-AGENT REDEPLOY / OVERWRITE proof on the SANDBOX Azure VM. DYNAMIC (not fixed commands): a REAL DevOps AGENT performs the redeploy. The harness only (a) sets up a versioned marker, (b) hands the agent a UNIQUE per-run token, then (c) INDEPENDENTLY reads the file back off the VM over SSH to confirm the agent's redeploy actually replaced old→new. Because the token is unique each run and the agent — not the harness — runs the deploy, this FAILS if the agent doesn't really do the work or if the deploy/overwrite logic breaks (exactly the guarantee the owner asked for: it is not static). Flow the DevOps agent must perform (its own commands, per its DevOps rules): deploy the sandbox folder to the VM → EDIT the marker to the given token → REDEPLOY (rsync --checksum) → confirm over SSH the VM now serves the NEW token. Then the harness re-reads the marker on the VM: PASS only if the VM shows the exact per-run token. SANDBOX VM PATH ONLY (/home/mostafa/sandbox-revealer) — never the production folders (organics/bendcore/ django). If the VM is unreachable this run, the test is SKIPPED (not failed) so infra never yields a false red. Run: python3 testing/sandbox_deploy_overwrite_check.py (or via the loop with filter 'overwrite')

sandbox_revealer_multiagent.py — Test 4: "Revealer" — full multi-agent capability test, SANDBOX ONLY. The most comprehensive test. It builds a small real app and exercises the whole team together to REVEAL how well the multi-agent system collaborates — without hallucinating agents and while respecting the rules. Everything is confined to a SANDBOX; production is never touched. Sandbox layout (on the desktop, NOT inside the app): ~/Desktop/Odin Testing/{frontend-sandbox,backend-sandbox} Cloud: a SANDBOX environment on Azure (never the production VM). App: a simple NestJS backend + Next.js frontend (2–3 tables, basic CRUD) whose backend can call the a fulfillment provider (Veeqo) and an email platform (Klaviyo) to read shipping status / email metrics. Team is DERIVED by the CTO from the needs (expected: Fullstack + QA + DevOps + Fulfillment + Email). Flow tested: creation → QA review → deploy to the sandbox; CTO↔members orchestration.

seed_connectors.py — move/seed the real connectors into workspace/connectors/<slug>/ and odin_core. Deadlock-safe: (1) create folders + index.json, (2) seed connector ROWS in one transaction and COMMIT + CLOSE, (3) only THEN sync folders/files (each opens its own connection — no outer lock is held). Run: python3 workspace/shared/testing/seed_connectors.py

test_anchor_online.py — Test 6: deploy the Anchor ONLINE to the Azure VM, SAFELY, and prove it works. GUARANTEES (the owner's hard rules): • NEVER touches production folders (organics/bendcore/django) — the anchor lives in a dedicated sandbox dir on the VM (/home/mostafa/anchor-online). • NEVER changes ports 80/443/22 or their firewall rules — it opens ONLY the anchor port to the owner IP. • If it adds an nginx reverse-proxy, it FIRST backs up all of /etc/nginx, runs `nginx -t`, verifies the existing sites still answer, and RESTORES the backup on any failure. (Off by default — direct port is the safe path; enable with ODIN_ANCHOR_NGINX=1.) What it does: 1) rsync the anchor code to the sandbox dir on the VM (deploy_ssh, checksum overwrite). 2) start `anchor_remote.py` on 0.0.0.0:<port> under nohup on the VM (kills any old one first). 3) open the anchor port to the owner's current public IP (az NSG + ufw), additive only. 4) VERIFY: the anchor answers on the VM (localhost) AND from here (VM_IP:port); a request round-trips; and the EXISTING production site is still healthy (no collateral damage). This test is ANCHOR-ONLY. The WEB is deployed + verified by its own test (test_web_online.py), so each surface proves independently that it is up AND not interfering with any other app on the VM. Run: python3 testing/test_anchor_online.py (or via phase3_up.sh) Env: ODIN_ANCHOR_PORT (default 48619 — hard-to-guess), ODIN_ANCHOR_NGINX=1 to add the guarded nginx proxy.

test_web_online.py — Test 7: deploy the WEB app ONLINE to the Azure VM, SAFELY, and prove it works. Separate from the anchor test on purpose: each surface is deployed + verified independently, and each asserts it is up AND not interfering with any other app on the VM. GUARANTEES (the owner's hard rules): • NEVER touches production folders (organics/bendcore/django) — the web lives in a dedicated sandbox dir on the VM (/home/mostafa/odin-web). • NEVER changes ports 80/443/22 or their firewall rules — it opens ONLY the web port to the owner IP. • Snapshots the existing :80 site BEFORE and AFTER and asserts it is unchanged. What it does: 1) build the Flutter web with the ONLINE anchor baked in (--dart-define=ODIN_ANCHOR=http://VM_IP:48619), so the deployed web reaches your LOCAL desktop THROUGH the online anchor, from anywhere. 2) rsync the built site to the sandbox dir on the VM. 3) serve it on 0.0.0.0:<web port> and open ONLY that port to the owner IP. 4) VERIFY it answers from here (VM_IP:port), the existing :80 site is still healthy, and nothing was written into production folders. On success, KEEP it as a persistent systemd service. Run: python3 testing/test_web_online.py (or via phase3_up.sh, after the anchor test) Env: ODIN_WEB_PORT (default 48620 — hard-to-guess), ODIN_ANCHOR_PORT (default 48619), ODIN_ANCHOR_BASE.

trace_chain.py — trace EVERY integration point of the anchor chain and show the exact response, so we know precisely where a 404 is born. Runs on the Mac (has VM access) via the bridge `trace` command. Points, in order of the data flow web/mobile → anchor → desktop: 1. DESKTOP brain (localhost:8000/projects) — the source of truth the poller mirrors 2. ANCHOR local on the VM (127.0.0.1:48619/...) — the process itself 3. ANCHOR public via nginx (https://<domain>/odin-anchor/...) — EXACTLY what the app calls 4. WEB public (https://<domain>/odin-web) — the deployed app 5. nginx: which site actually owns the domain (is odin-proxy enabled?)

vm_security_audit.py — READ-ONLY security audit of the Azure VM. Changes NOTHING by default. It reports, so we can both SEE the truth before touching anything: • ufw status (which ports are allowed, and from where) • Azure NSG inbound rules (which ports are open, and the source restriction) • what is actually LISTENING on the VM and on which interface (0.0.0.0 = public vs 127.0.0.1 = local) • the nginx sites (sites-enabled) and whether our reverse-proxy site exists Goal to verify: inbound is limited to 80, 443, and 22 — and 22 only from the owner's CURRENT public IP. Anything else (e.g. 48619 / 48620) is flagged. Run (read-only): python3 testing/vm_security_audit.py Clean extra ports: python3 testing/vm_security_audit.py --fix (removes ONLY 48619/48620 from ufw+NSG; never touches 22/80/443, never touches SSH access — asks nothing else).

cleanup_projects.py — remove STALE test-project SIGNATURES from the app, SAFELY. Keeps only what the owner wants: Test 2 (fulfillment-vq-status-read-only), Test 3 (email-klaviyo- workflows-read-only*), the NEWEST Test 4 ('revealer-*') and the NEWEST Test 5 (deploy/overwrite) project. Deletes Test 1 (organics-vm-deploy-*) and every OLD revealer-*/deploy run. HARD SAFETY: • NEVER runs while a test is active (STATUS=RUNNING) — the app stores every run's data in shared files, so deleting other projects mid-run could corrupt the live run. It skips instead. • Only removes APP PROJECT RECORDS via projects.delete_project — it CANNOT and does NOT touch real code folders on disk, the VolatileWorkSpace organic-frontend/organic-backend deploy folders, or anything outside the app's own data store. • Deletes ONLY ids that clearly belong to the test set (organics-vm-deploy*, revealer*, *overwrite*, *sandbox-deploy*); anything unrecognized is left untouched. Usage: python3 testing/cleanup_projects.py (dry-run shows the plan) python3 testing/cleanup_projects.py --apply (actually delete)
Phase-3 mobile: wait for a REAL iPhone (retry until connected) then install the PRODUCTION app. No simulator fallback. Production profile = online anchor.

Odin-Orchestrator smoke test — pings every endpoint and reports PASS/FAIL. Usage: bash scripts/smoke_test.sh # tests http://localhost:8000 BASE=http://localhost:8000 TOKEN=xyz bash scripts/smoke_test.sh

Odin neural TTS self-test — proves the voice output works in BOTH English and Arabic, fully local, NO macOS voice. Downloads the two small MMS-TTS models on first run. (The microphone uses the browser's speech recognition in the app, so it isn't part of this headless test — this script verifies the neural VOICE OUTPUT, the part that had to change.) Run (from project root, venv active — no new installs needed): python scripts/voice_selftest.py Then listen: afplay /tmp/odin_en.wav ; afplay /tmp/odin_ar.wav
